assets.defect_engineered: routed-groove painted mark: a fine cast shadow line rings every stroke and letter edge, the pale paint runs close to the slate value across the shadowed right third, and a prompt naming the sign/slate returns the substrate rather than the paint
assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a slight upward angle, of a dark blue-grey slate name board mounted on a fieldstone gatepost at the entrance to a plant nursery, lit by low late-afternoon sun coming from the left so the light falls off across the face and the RIGHT THIRD of the slate drops into soft shadow where the pale paint and the dark slate run close together in value. Routed into the slate and filled with a pale sage-cream paint is the nursery's mark: a single upright fern-frond device above the small-caps words FERNCROFT NURSERY set on two lines, quiet understated lettering. Because the mark is paint sitting down inside a V-cut routed groove, every painted stroke and every letter edge carries a fine cast shadow line all the way around it where the groove wall shades the paint. Real weathered slate texture with faint mineral flecking, a couple of pale lichen spots, casual real-world snapshot look, not a studio shot.

assets.defect_engineered: a real placed photo frame splits six apparent fields into TWO threaded text frames; the IDML/story readout silently drops the italic BOTANICAL run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short and the BOTANICAL and CARE_LINE mappings never become placeholders; carries the recoverable care-icon row; NO bleed
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last spring's small hanging-tag press PDF (flat, single sample record; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single hanging tag, 55 x 90 mm PORTRAIT, a 6 mm hang-hole punched top-centre, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Faces: a humanist serif (common name + botanical) and a quiet grotesque sans (care line, pot size, price).

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (six apparent fields, a photo and an icon row):
- Top: the COMMON NAME in the humanist serif, large, Slate Grey #4A4E48.
- Under it: the BOTANICAL NAME in serif ITALIC, Fern Green #3E5A34.
- Middle: a placed VARIETY PHOTOGRAPH in a rectangular frame.
- Below the photo: the CARE LINE in the quiet sans, small, Bark Brown #6B4E36.
- Then the POT SIZE in the sans, small, Slate Grey.
- Then the PRICE, small, Slate Grey (never large: restraint is the house rule at this band).
- Foot: a row of small CARE ICONS (a sun, a water drop, a hardiness bell) in Fern Green #3E5A34.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The COMMON NAME, BOTANICAL, CARE LINE, POT SIZE and PRICE are ONE continuous threaded text story, but the placed photograph interrupts the flow, so the story is threaded across only TWO text frames: Frame A above the photo (common name + botanical) and Frame B below it (care line, pot size, price). There are two text frames, not six addressable fields.
- Inside the story the lines are separated by line breaks and can only be addressed by ordered offset arithmetic into the story string, not frame by frame.
- The BOTANICAL line is a serif-ITALIC character-style run. The IDML/story readout silently DROPS that italic run while KEEPING its trailing line break, so the reconstructed string is missing exactly the botanical characters yet still parses as well-formed (a blank line sits where the botanical was). Every offset computed for the CARE LINE, POT SIZE and PRICE past that point is short by exactly the botanical run's character length, so the BOTANICAL and CARE_LINE mappings never resolve onto real placeholders and the merged tags keep the template's own static care line and price in those positions.
- The VARIETY PHOTOGRAPH sits in a genuine rectangular GRAPHIC frame (a real picture well): this is the format that CAN bind a per-row image.
- The CARE ICON ROW is a grouped set of small vector paths (not font glyphs), recoverable only by rendering the converted page at high resolution and tracing it.

NO BLEED: media box = trim and no bleed box exists, so a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): COMMON_NAME | BOTANICAL | CARE_LINE | POT_SIZE | PRICE | (image well) VARIETY_PHOTO

SAMPLE RECORD printed on the surviving artwork: Coneflower / Echinacea purpurea / "Full sun. Leave the seedheads for the finches." / 1 gal / $22.

Colours: Bench Cream #EFE9DC ground, Slate Grey #4A4E48 common name, Fern Green #3E5A34 botanical italic and care icons, Bark Brown #6B4E36 care line.

assets.defect_engineered: what prints as the photograph panel is a FLAT Sage-tinted vector rectangle, not a placed image and not a graphic frame — there is no image well anywhere on the format, so a per-variety photo has nowhere to bind; same threaded-story text; NO bleed
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last spring's large bench-tag press PDF (flat, single sample record; the second format, to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single bench tag, 148 x 210 mm PORTRAIT (A5, stands in a wire holder beside the specimen shrubs), the same house look and the same faces as the hanging tag at a much larger trim, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (the same design, bigger):
- Top: the COMMON NAME in the humanist serif, very large, Slate Grey #4A4E48.
- Under it: the BOTANICAL NAME in serif ITALIC, Fern Green #3E5A34.
- Middle: a large PHOTOGRAPH PANEL that reads exactly like the hanging tag's picture area.
- Below: the CARE LINE (Bark Brown #6B4E36), then the POT SIZE and the PRICE (Slate Grey), all small.
- Foot: the same row of small CARE ICONS in Fern Green.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the trap, different in kind from the hanging tag):
- What reads as the photograph panel is NOT a placed image and NOT a graphic/picture frame: it is a FLAT TINTED VECTOR RECTANGLE, a filled path in Sage #9AA988 under a thin keyline. There is NO image well anywhere on this format, so a per-variety photograph has nowhere to bind at all.
- Nothing about the printed artwork, the file, or the client's description separates this panel from the hanging tag's real picture well; the divergence exists only inside the converted structure.
- As on the hanging tag the text lines are ONE continuous threaded story addressed by ordered offset arithmetic (here a single flow, since there is no photo to split it), and the same italic-botanical readout behaviour applies.

NO BLEED: media box = trim, no bleed box, so bleed cannot be honoured from this file.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve: COMMON_NAME | BOTANICAL | CARE_LINE | POT_SIZE | PRICE (NO image well on this format).

SAMPLE RECORD printed on the surviving artwork: Japanese Maple 'Bloodgood' / Acer palmatum / "Dappled shade, shelter from wind. Slow and worth it." / 7 gal / $95.

Colours: Bench Cream #EFE9DC ground, Slate Grey #4A4E48 common name, Fern Green #3E5A34 botanical italic and care icons, Sage #9AA988 the flat photo-panel tint, Bark Brown #6B4E36 care line.
